19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
74	- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
75	- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
76	- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
77	- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开
78	
79	### 2.3 审稿人视角检验
80	
81	写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
82	- 问题是否重要？
83	- 方法是否清楚？
84	- 贡献是否可信？
85	- 结果是否有说服力？
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 三、Introduction 写作规范
90	
91	### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）
92	
93	Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：
94	
95	1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
96	2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
97	3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
98	4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
99	5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献
100	
101	### 3.2 整体叙事结构
102	
103	```
104	现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
105	```
106	
107	### 3.3 禁忌
108	
109	- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
110	- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
111	- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
112	- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
113	- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 四、Related Work 写作规范
118	
119	### 4.1 目标
120	
121	让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。
122	
123	### 4.2 结构要求
124	
125	- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
126	- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
127	- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口
128	
129	### 4.3 禁忌
130	
131	- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
132	- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
133	- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work
134	
135	### 4.4 引用充足度
136	
137	- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
138	- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
139	- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）
144	
145	以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**
146	
147	### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）
148	
149	**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**
150	
151	- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
152	- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
153	- 强制检查命令：
154	  ```bash
155	  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
156	  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
157	  ```
158	- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）
159	
160	### 5.2 段落与句式
161	
162	- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
163	- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
164	- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
165	- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
166	- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容
167	
168	### 5.3 用词黑名单
169	
170	- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
171	- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
172	- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
173	- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用
174	
175	### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）
176	
177	1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
178	2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
179	3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
180	4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 六、图表与视觉规范
185	
186	### 6.1 知识密度原则
187	
188	- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
189	- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
190	- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure
191	
192	### 6.2 表格规范
193	
194	- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
195	- 小数精度全表统一
196	- 最优加粗、次优下划线
197	- Caption 必须自包含
198	
199	### 6.3 图片规范
200	
201	- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
202	- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
203	- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
204	- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页
205	
206	### 6.4 空间效率
207	
208	- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
209	- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
210	- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
211	- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比
212	
213	### 6.5 页面节奏
214	
215	好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：
216	
217	- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
218	- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
219	- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
220	- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
221	- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）
222	
223	### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范
224	
225	**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
226	- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
227	- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
228	- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
229	- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
230	- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）
231	
232	**宽度决策树**：
233	- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
234	- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
235	- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix
236	
237	---
238	
239	## 七、投稿前通用准备
240	
241	### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）
242	
243	- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
244	- **不要用**：
245	  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
246	  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
247	  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
248	- 风险：
249	  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
250	  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
251	  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
252	- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
253	- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致
254	
255	### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对
256	
257	- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
258	- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
259	- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
260	- 行号开启（review 版常需）
261	- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件
262	
263	### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程
264	
265	提交前必须逐一检查：
266	1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
267	2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
268	3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
269	4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
270	5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
271	6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
272	7. 所有专有名词有定义
273	8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
274	9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
275	10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础

- 方法是否清楚？
- 贡献是否可信？
- 结果是否有说服力？

---

## 三、Introduction 写作规范

### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）

Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：

1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

### 3.2 整体叙事结构

```
现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
```

### 3.3 禁忌

- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念

---

## 四、Related Work 写作规范

### 4.1 目标

让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。

### 4.2 结构要求

- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口

### 4.3 禁忌

- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work

### 4.4 引用充足度

- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足

---

## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）

以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**

### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）

**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**

- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
- 强制检查命令：
  ```bash
  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
  ```
- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）

### 5.2 段落与句式

- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容

### 5.3 用词黑名单

- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用

### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）

1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写

---

## 六、图表与视觉规范

### 6.1 知识密度原则

- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure

### 6.2 表格规范

- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
- 小数精度全表统一
- 最优加粗、次优下划线
- Caption 必须自包含

### 6.3 图片规范

- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页

### 6.4 空间效率

- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比

### 6.5 页面节奏

好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：

- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）

### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范

**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）

**宽度决策树**：
- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix

---

## 七、投稿前通用准备

### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）

- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
- **不要用**：
  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
- 风险：
  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致

### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对

- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
- 行号开启（review 版常需）
- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件

### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程

提交前必须逐一检查：
1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
7. 所有专有名词有定义
8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础

17	# LaTeX 论文写作全流程
18	
19	ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。
20	
21	---
22	
23	## 1. 工作模式
24	
25	开始前选择模式：
26	
27	| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
28	|------|------|------|
29	| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
30	| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
31	| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论
36	
37	**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**
38	
39	### 2.1 一句话贡献
40	
41	在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。
42	
43	### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map
44	
45	为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：
46	
47	| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
48	|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
49	| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
50	| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
51	| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |
52	
53	**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**
54	
55	### 2.3 章节起草顺序
56	
57	```
58	1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
59	2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
60	3. Related Work
61	4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
62	```
63	
64	### 2.4 Quality Gates
65	
66	投稿前必须通过：
67	- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
68	- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
69	- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
70	- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
71	- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta
72	
73	---
74	
75	## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）
76	
77	**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**
78	
79	### 3.1 黄金法则
80	
81	```
82	IF 无法程序化获取引用:
83	    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
84	    → 明确告知用户
85	    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
86	```
87	
88	### 3.2 五步验证流程
89	
90	```
91	1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
92	2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
93	3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
94	4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
95	5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
96	```
97	
98	### 3.3 API 速查
99	
100	| API | 用途 | 限制 |
101	|-----|------|------|
102	| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
103	| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
104	| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |
105	
106	```python
107	# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
108	import requests
109	def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
110	    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
111	                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
112	    r.raise_for_status()
113	    return r.text
114	
115	# Semantic Scholar 搜索
116	from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
117	sch = SemanticScholar()
118	results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
119	for p in results:
120	    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
121	```
122	
123	### 3.4 引用处理规则
124	
125	| 情况 | 处理 |
126	|------|------|
127	| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
128	| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
129	| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
130	| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
131	| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |
132	
133	---
134	
135	## 4. 顶会模板速查
136	
137	### 4.1 ML/AI 会议
138	
139	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
140	|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
141	| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
142	| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
143	| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
144	| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
145	| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
146	| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |
147	
148	### 4.2 系统会议
149	
150	| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
151	|------|---------|---------|---------|
152	| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
153	| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
154	| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
155	| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |
156	
157	### 4.3 模板使用原则
158	
159	```bash
160	# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
161	cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/
162	
163	# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
164	latexmk -pdf main.tex
165	
166	# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
167	```
168	
169	**禁止事项：**
170	- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
171	- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
172	- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`
173	
174	---
175	
176	## 5. 写作规范
177	
178	### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）
179	
180	花**大致相等**的时间在：
181	1. Abstract
182	2. Introduction
183	3. 图表
184	4. **其余所有内容加起来**
185	
186	审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。
187	
188	### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）
189	
190	```
191	1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
192	2. 为什么这很难且重要
193	3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
194	4. 有什么证据
195	5. 最惊人的数字/结果
196	```
197	
198	删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~
199	
200	### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）
201	
202	| 原则 | 规则 |
203	|------|------|
204	| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
205	| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
206	| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
207	| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |
208	
209	### 5.4 常见修改
210	
211	| 问题 | 修复 |
212	|------|------|
213	| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
214	| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
215	| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
216	| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |
217	
218	---
219	
220	## 6. 投稿工程链
221	
222	### 6.1 构建
223	
224	```bash
225	# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
226	latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex
227	
228	# 手动：需要多次编译
229	pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
230	```
231	
232	### 6.2 Lint + 格式化
233	
234	```bash
235	# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
236	chktex main.tex
237	
238	# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
239	latexindent -w main.tex
240	```
241	
242	### 6.3 图表格式
243	
244	| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
245	|------|------|------|
246	| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
247	| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
248	| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |
249	
250	```latex
251	\usepackage{booktabs}
252	\begin{tabular}{lcc}
253	\toprule
254	Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
255	\midrule
256	Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
257	\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
258	\bottomrule
259	\end{tabular}
260	```
261	
262	**图表规范：**
263	- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
264	- 图内不放标题（用 caption）

# LaTeX 论文写作全流程

ML/AI 顶会论文从草稿到投稿的完整指南。整合 Orchestra Research、VibeSkills、claim2evidence 三方最佳实践。

---

## 1. 工作模式

开始前选择模式：

| 模式 | 说明 | 适用 |
|------|------|------|
| **Build** | 从实验笔记/结果/代码生成论文 | 新稿 |
| **Improve** | 改写已有章节，强化论证 | 修改稿 |
| **Audit** | 输出风险列表 + 缺失证据 + 修复建议 | 投前检查 |

---

## 2. Claim-Evidence 方法论

**核心原则：论文是一个有中心贡献的故事，不是实验的堆砌。**

### 2.1 一句话贡献

在写任何内容之前，必须能用一句话说清贡献。如果不能，说明还没准备好写论文。

### 2.2 Claim-Evidence Map

为每个 contribution 建立 claim→evidence 映射表：

| Contribution | Claim | Evidence | Table/Figure |
|-------------|-------|----------|-------------|
| C1: 方法 X 在 Y 上 SOTA | 比所有 baseline 高 ≥2% | 5-seed 平均，p<0.05 | Table 1 |
| C2: 消融证明 Z 是关键 | 去掉 Z 后掉 >5% | 消融实验 | Table 2 |
| C3: 计算效率 | 比 baseline 快 3× | FLOPs + wall-clock | Figure 3 |

**没有直接证据支撑的 claim 必须删除或降级为 discussion。**

### 2.3 章节起草顺序

```
1. Introduction + Experiments（先确定 claim 和 evidence）
2. Method（评估问题稳定后再写细节）
3. Related Work
4. Abstract + Title（核心 claim 定型后最后写）
```

### 2.4 Quality Gates

投稿前必须通过：
- [ ] 前两段出现显式 novelty 声明
- [ ] 每个 contribution 有可验证的 evidence
- [ ] Abstract / Intro / Conclusion 的 claim 一致
- [ ] Limitations 真实且技术性诚实
- [ ] 审稿人两分钟内能识别 delta

---

## 3. 引用防幻觉（CRITICAL）

**AI 生成引用有 ~40% 错误率。绝对禁止凭记忆写 BibTeX。**

### 3.1 黄金法则

```
IF 无法程序化获取引用:
    → 标记 [CITATION NEEDED] 或 \cite{PLACEHOLDER_verify}
    → 明确告知用户
    → 绝不编造看似合理的引用
```

### 3.2 五步验证流程

```
1. SEARCH  → Semantic Scholar API 搜索关键词
2. VERIFY  → 至少 2 个来源确认论文存在（S2 + arXiv/CrossRef）
3. RETRIEVE → 通过 DOI 获取 BibTeX（程序化，非记忆）
4. CHECK   → 确认你引用的 claim 确实出自该论文
5. ADD     → 加入 .bib 文件
```

### 3.3 API 速查

| API | 用途 | 限制 |
|-----|------|------|
| **Semantic Scholar** | ML/AI 论文搜索 | 1 RPS (免费) |
| **CrossRef** | DOI → BibTeX | 需 mailto 头 |
| **arXiv** | 预印本搜索 | 3s 间隔 |

```python
# DOI → BibTeX（最可靠的方式）
import requests
def doi_to_bibtex(doi: str) -> str:
    r = requests.get(f"https://doi.org/{doi}",
                     headers={"Accept": "application/x-bibtex"})
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.text

# Semantic Scholar 搜索
from semanticscholar import SemanticScholar
sch = SemanticScholar()
results = sch.search_paper("attention mechanism transformers", limit=5)
for p in results:
    print(f"{p.title} | DOI: {p.externalIds.get('DOI', 'N/A')}")
```

### 3.4 引用处理规则

| 情况 | 处理 |
|------|------|
| 找到论文 + DOI + BibTeX | 直接用 |
| 找到论文，无 DOI | 用 arXiv BibTeX |
| 论文存在但无法获取 BibTeX | 标记 placeholder，告知用户 |
| 不确定论文是否存在 | 标记 `[CITATION NEEDED]`，告知用户 |
| "我觉得有篇关于 X 的论文" | **绝不引用** — 先搜索或标记 |

---

## 4. 顶会模板速查

### 4.1 ML/AI 会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 主文件 | 样式文件 | 必须项 |
|------|---------|--------|---------|--------|
| **NeurIPS** | 9 页 | `main.tex` | `neurips.sty` | Paper Checklist |
| **ICML** | 8 页 (+1 camera-ready) | `example_paper.tex` | `icml2026.sty` | Broader Impact |
| **ICLR** | 9 页 (+1) | `iclr_conference.tex` | `iclr_conference.sty` | LLM 使用声明 |
| **ACL/EMNLP** | 8 页 (long) | `acl_latex.tex` | `acl.sty` | Limitations 必须 |
| **AAAI** | 7 页 (+1) | `aaai_template.tex` | `aaai.sty` | 严格样式 |
| **COLM** | 9 页 (+1) | `colm_conference.tex` | `colm_conference.sty` | 语言模型聚焦 |

### 4.2 系统会议

| 会议 | 页数限制 | 模板类型 | 关键要求 |
|------|---------|---------|---------|
| **OSDI** | 12 页 (+2) | USENIX `usenix.sty` | Research / Operational 双 track |
| **NSDI** | 12 页 | USENIX | Introduction 预筛 |
| **ASPLOS** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 前 2 页快速评审 |
| **SOSP** | 12 页 | ACM `acmart.cls (sigplan)` | 可选 Artifact Evaluation |

### 4.3 模板使用原则

```bash
# 1. 复制整个模板目录（不要只拷 .tex）
cp -r templates/neurips2025/ ~/papers/my-paper/

# 2. 先编译未修改的模板，确认能跑通
latexmk -pdf main.tex

# 3. 逐章替换内容，频繁编译
```

**禁止事项：**
- 不要修改 `.sty` 文件
- 不要在会议模板间复制 `\usepackage` 行
- 不要只复制 `.tex` 而不带 `.sty/.bst`

---

## 5. 写作规范

### 5.1 时间分配（Neel Nanda）

花**大致相等**的时间在：
1. Abstract
2. Introduction
3. 图表
4. **其余所有内容加起来**

审稿人读论文的顺序：标题 → 摘要 → 引言 → 图表 → 也许正文。

### 5.2 Abstract 五句法（Sebastian Farquhar）

```
1. 你做了什么（"We introduce/prove/demonstrate..."）
2. 为什么这很难且重要
3. 怎么做的（含专业关键词以便检索）
4. 有什么证据
5. 最惊人的数字/结果
```

删除一切泛泛的开头：~~"Large language models have achieved remarkable success..."~~

### 5.3 句子级清晰度（Gopen & Swan）

| 原则 | 规则 |
|------|------|
| 主谓紧邻 | 不要在主语和动词之间插入长从句 |
| 重点在句尾 | 把关键数字/结论放在句末 |
| 旧信息在前 | 先放读者已知的内容，再引入新概念 |
| 动词表达动作 | "We analyzed" 而非 "We performed an analysis" |

### 5.4 常见修改

| 问题 | 修复 |
|------|------|
| Abstract 太泛 | 删第一句（如果它能放在任何 ML 论文前面） |
| Introduction 超 1.5 页 | 背景挪到 Related Work |
| 实验没有显式 claim | 每个实验前加 "This tests whether..." |
| 缺统计显著性 | 加 error bars + 运行次数 + 计算方法 |

---

## 6. 投稿工程链

### 6.1 构建

```bash
# 推荐：latexmk 一键构建
latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex

# 手动：需要多次编译
pdflatex main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex main.tex && pdflatex main.tex
```

### 6.2 Lint + 格式化

```bash
# Lint: 检查常见 LaTeX 问题
chktex main.tex

# 格式化: 减少 diff 噪声
latexindent -w main.tex
```

### 6.3 图表格式

| 类型 | 格式 | 说明 |
|------|------|------|
| 矢量图（plot、diagram） | PDF | matplotlib: `plt.savefig('fig.pdf')` |
| 照片/heatmap | PNG 600dpi 或 TIFF | 栅格图 |
| 表格 | `booktabs` 包 | `\toprule/\midrule/\bottomrule` |

```latex
\usepackage{booktabs}
\begin{tabular}{lcc}
\toprule
Method & Accuracy $\uparrow$ & Latency $\downarrow$ \\
\midrule
Baseline & 85.2 & 45ms \\
\textbf{Ours} & \textbf{92.1} & 38ms \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
```

**图表规范：**
- 用色盲友好色板（Okabe-Ito 或 Paul Tol）
- 图内不放标题（用 caption）
- Caption 独立可理解（不依赖正文）
- 最佳值加粗，标注方向符号（↑ 越高越好，↓ 越低越好）

### 6.4 投稿打包

```bash
# 清理辅助文件
latexmk -c

# 打包投稿
zip -r submission.zip main.tex *.sty *.bst *.bib figures/ --exclude='*.aux' --exclude='*.log'
```

### 6.5 常见失败点

| 问题 | 解决 |
|------|------|
| 图片格式混用导致编译失败 | 统一用 PDF |
| 字体未嵌入 | `pdffonts output.pdf` 检查 |
| Overfull box 过多 | 关键位置手动调行 |
| 引用缺字段 | 检查 DOI/年份/期刊名 |
| 超页数 | 用 `\vspace{-Xpt}` 微调，或精简内容 |

---

## 7. 会议转投

当论文被拒或转投其他会议时：

### 7.1 ML/AI 会议间转换

| 转换 | 页数变化 | 关键调整 |
|------|---------|---------|
| NeurIPS → ICML | 9→8 | 删 1 页，加 Broader Impact |
| ICML → ICLR | 8→9 | 可扩展实验 + LLM 声明 |
| NeurIPS → ACL | 9→8 | 按 NLP 惯例重组 + Limitations |
| ICLR → AAAI | 9→7 | 大幅精简，严格样式 |

### 7.2 转投原则

1. **永远用目标模板重新开始** — 复制目标模板，迁移内容，不要合并 preamble
2. **只迁移正文内容** — 不复制 `\usepackage`、header/footer 命令
3. **根据审稿意见改进** — 但不要在新稿中提及旧投稿（双盲）
4. **检查目标会议特殊要求** — checklist、ethics statement、LLM 声明等

---

## 8. 投前清单

### 通用清单

- [ ] Abstract/Intro/Conclusion 的 claim 一致
- [ ] 每个 contribution 有对应 evidence
- [ ] 所有引用已程序化验证（无幻觉引用）
- [ ] Error bars + 运行次数 + 统计方法
- [ ] Limitations 章节存在且诚实
- [ ] 匿名化（双盲审稿）
- [ ] 符合页数限制
- [ ] 所有图表有自包含 caption
- [ ] `.bib` 中无缺失字段
- [ ] PDF 编译无 warning

### 会议特定

| ICML | Broader Impact Statement |

3	
4	What does fine-tuning change inside a Vision-Language-Action model (VLA)?
5	VLAs fine-tune large language models on robot demonstrations to produce actions from visual observations and language instructions~\cite{brohan2023_rt2,kim2024_openvla}, but the decoder-only causal mask prevents image tokens from attending to instructions~\cite{wang2025seeing,pei2025rethinking}.
6	Instruction information must reach action-generating positions through learned attention patterns, yet how fine-tuning reshapes these patterns remains uncharacterized.
7	
8	Recent behavioral studies reveal that VLAs rely disproportionately on visual input~\cite{grant2026}, with language instructions largely ignored by the action pathway~\cite{haon2025}.
9	These findings suggest internal specialization but do not explain \emph{how} instruction information reaches the action-generating readout token, \emph{what} attention strategy fine-tuning learns compared to language pretraining alone, or \emph{whether} training creates new representational structure or reconfigures inherited geometry.
10	Existing analyses have not combined systematic per-layer probing with factorial trained/pretrained/untrained controls, leaving the representational mechanisms of VLA fine-tuning opaque.
11	
12	We address this gap by decomposing OpenVLA-7B~\cite{kim2024_openvla,karamcheti2024}, a VLA chaining a frozen DinoSigLIP vision backbone~\cite{zhai2023_siglip,oquab2024_dinov2}, an MLP projector, and Llama-2 7B~\cite{touvron2023_llama2}.
13	We extract representations from each of 32 LLM layers at both image-token and readout-token positions, and from external baselines (DINOv2~\cite{oquab2024_dinov2}, CLIP~\cite{radford2021_clip}).
14	We compare three LLM conditions (VLA-trained, pretrained Llama-2 base, and randomly initialized) crossed with instruction presence, and apply four complementary analyses: cross-instruction probes for token-level specialization, L1 attention pattern analysis, RSA~\cite{kriegeskorte2008} for geometric alignment, and MLP probes~\cite{alain2017} for functional decodability.

21	(a)~Architecture overview.
22	(b)~Instruction-dominant heads per layer (L1 attention $>0.5$). Pretrained Llama-2 peaks at mid-depth; VLA-trained OpenVLA concentrates at L1 and L32. Untrained: zero heads at all layers.}

26	Three findings emerge.
27	\emph{First}, VLA fine-tuning redistributes instruction attention from mid-depth to entry-exit layers, supported by seven complementary analyses including dose-response and counterfactual ablation (\S\ref{sec:learned_routing}).
28	\emph{Second}, a $2{\times}2$ trained-vs-untrained comparison across two causal-decoder VLAs---OpenVLA (Llama-2) and TraceVLA (Phi-3-V), which start from dramatically different untrained profiles---reveals a consistent reorganization pattern: both reach similar mid-layer action-decodability peaks after training ($\Delta R^2 = 0.003$), with training effects concentrated at the readout token rather than image geometry (\S\ref{sec:nonmonotonic}).
29	If routing were purely architecture-specific, different backbones should not arrive at the same functional profile; the observed consistency across two architectures is compatible with VLA training discovering a common organization constrained by the causal-decoder design.

10	Each architecture is compared in trained and untrained conditions, with a critical asymmetry between untrained baselines: OpenVLA's untrained checkpoint is the OXE-pretrained~\cite{padalkar2023_oxe} VLA (already fine-tuned for action prediction on 970K episodes), while TracVLA and NORA untrained checkpoints are pure vision-language models (Phi-3-Vision and Qwen2.5-VL) with no action training.
11	Three analyses are applied to each cell (\S\ref{sec:method}): $R^2$ action probes at all layers, L1 attention head profiling for instruction dominance, and counterfactual instruction perturbation.
12	For OpenVLA LIBERO-Goal, $N = 63{,}228$ observations; other cells are at comparable scale.
13	For trained models that produce action outputs, counterfactual sensitivity is measured via Cohen's $d$ on action MSE.
14	For untrained VLMs (Phi-3-Vision, Qwen2.5-VL) that do not produce actions, sensitivity is measured via cosine distance on hidden representations; these metrics operate on different scales and are not directly comparable (\S\ref{sec:cf_sensitivity}).
15	OpenVLA's OXE-pretrained checkpoint produces actions, permitting same-metric (Cohen's $d$) comparison in that condition.
16	Bonferroni correction details appear in Appendix~\ref{sec:bonferroni_correction}.

18	%------------------------------------------------------------------
19	\subsection{OpenVLA: Instruction Routing and Functional Sensitivity}
20	\label{sec:openvla_routing}
21	
22	We first establish the core phenomena on a single architecture before testing cross-architectural generality.
23	Cross-instruction probes validate the analysis framework on OpenVLA~\cite{kim2024_openvla}: as predicted by the causal mask, image\_mean instruction classification stays at chance ($10\%$) across all 32 layers in all conditions (full profile in Appendix~\ref{sec:dense_routing}).
24	Trained readout achieves $100\%$ 10-way classification from L1 onward and maintains this through L31 (LOOCV-confirmed; Appendix~\ref{sec:loocv}).
25	Untrained readout also reaches $100\%$ at L1 but decays to $82\%$ by L31; the readout token is thus the primary multimodal integration site, and training stabilizes its instruction encoding across depth.
26	All patterns reproduce with a linear probe (Appendix~\ref{sec:linear_probe}).
27	
28	At L1, three conditions form a gradient of instruction attention: untrained networks allocate 0/32 instruction-dominant heads ($11.7\%$ text attention, $1.5\times$ text-to-image ratio), Llama-2 base~\cite{touvron2023_llama2} allocates 9/32 ($36.5\%$), and VLA-trained allocates 24/32 ($57.7\%$, $38.2\times$ text-to-image ratio; Appendix~\ref{sec:attention_decomp}).
29	The 32-layer attention profile reveals qualitatively distinct organizations: Llama-2 base concentrates instruction attention at mid-depth (L9--L16: 15--22 heads), while VLA fine-tuning produces an entry-exit bookend pattern with L0--L1 at 21--24 heads, L31 at 18, and intermediate layers at 0--11 (Appendix~\ref{sec:threshold_sensitivity}).
30	Head counts are computed at a $50\%$ threshold; sensitivity analysis ($30\%$--$70\%$) confirms ordering robustness.
31	A fourth condition, OpenVLA fine-tuned on LIBERO, preserves L1 entry concentration (22/32 heads) but loses L31 exit re-engagement entirely (0 vs.\ 18 heads for the OXE-pretrained model), consistent with exit-layer attention serving multi-task flexibility rather than task-specific routing.
32	The redistribution beyond Llama-2 base priors confirms that VLA fine-tuning creates new instruction routing rather than merely inheriting language-model attention.
33	
34	Counterfactual instruction perturbation validates the functional relevance of these structural patterns.
35	Four perturbation types across 10 LIBERO-Goal tasks produce action divergence ordered by token novelty ($\rho = 0.8$): empty instruction ($d = 0.978$), wrong task ($0.924$), shuffled tokens ($0.763$), paraphrased ($0.707$).
36	The shuffled-exceeds-paraphrased ordering, despite identical token sets, indicates that positional sensitivity dominates token-level novelty.
37	The effect replicates across LIBERO-Spatial (10 tasks) with the same ordering: empty $0.942$, wrong $0.851$, shuffled $0.833$, paraphrased $0.806$ (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:counterfactual_spatial}).
38	Across both suites (20 tasks), the gradient spans $d = 0.71$--$0.98$.
39	Spatial instructions differ only in prepositions, yet wrong-task perturbation still produces $d = 0.851$; instruction-dominant heads route fine-grained spatial information, not merely task identity.
40	
41	Dose-response ablation of L1 instruction-dominant heads produces monotonic trajectory divergence: $d$ rises from $0.482$ to $0.639$ as 4--32 heads are progressively ablated, with steep increase through 12 heads and plateau beyond 20 (Appendix~\ref{sec:action_trajectory}).
42	Ablating all 24 instruction-dominant heads alters $72.3\%$ of action tokens (token-level $d = 0.65$, trajectory-level $d = 2.943$); control ablation of 8 random heads yields $d = 0.41$ ($29.3\%$ tokens affected), concentrated on the gripper dimension.
43	The routing effect is task-dependent: instruction-discriminative tasks show $2.5\times$ larger $|\Delta R^2|$ under L1 ablation than visually-sufficient tasks ($p = 0.033$; Appendix~\ref{sec:task_complexity}).
44	$R^2$ action probing localizes training effects: trained readout peaks at $R^2 = 0.678$ (L13), untrained readout peaks at $0.609$ (L32), and the training effect concentrates at the readout ($+0.069$) rather than at image\_mean ($+0.015$; Appendix~\ref{sec:action_r2_threecond}).
45	These effects survive Bonferroni correction across all 63 tests (Appendix~\ref{sec:bonferroni_correction}).
46	The single-architecture analysis establishes three phenomena for cross-architectural testing: instruction-dominant attention at L1, $R^2$ exit-layer dynamics between trained and untrained conditions, and graded counterfactual sensitivity to instruction perturbation.
47

49	\subsection{Cross-Architecture $R^2$ Exit Collapse}
50	\label{sec:r2_collapse}
51	
52	We define $R^2$ exit collapse as the drop in action-probe $R^2$ from peak layer to exit layer ($\Delta R^2 = R^2_{\text{peak}} - R^2_{\text{exit}}$).
53	A large $\Delta R^2$ indicates that action-relevant information encoded at intermediate layers is selectively discarded or transformed before reaching the exit.
54	Table~\ref{tab:cross_arch_matrix} reports this quantity for all available cells in the $3 \times 4$ matrix.
55	A consistent pattern emerges: trained models exhibit substantially larger $\Delta R^2$ than their untrained counterparts, but the magnitude and prevalence of collapse depend on the training transition being measured.
56	
57	TracVLA~\cite{zheng2024tracevla} shows clear exit collapse across all four LIBERO suites.
58	Trained $\Delta R^2$ ranges from $0.138$ (Spatial: peak $R^2 = 0.809$, exit $0.671$) to $0.294$ (Object: peak $0.764$, exit $0.470$), while untrained $\Delta R^2$ is uniformly small, from $0.009$ (Object) to $0.048$ (Goal).
59	The untrained TracVLA checkpoint is Phi-3-Vision, a pure vision-language model with no action training, and its flat $R^2$ profiles confirm that exit collapse is absent before VLA fine-tuning.
60	NORA~\cite{TODO_nora} exhibits the most extreme collapse in the matrix.
61	LIBERO-Goal trained produces $\Delta R^2 = 0.691$: the profile peaks at $R^2 = 0.688$ in mid-layers and drops to $-0.004$ at exit, below chance, so exit-layer representations encode less action-relevant structure than random vectors.
62	LIBERO-Spatial yields $\Delta R^2 = 0.302$ (peak $0.720$, exit $0.417$).
63	NORA untrained (Qwen2.5-VL) produces $\Delta R^2$ of only $0.044$ and $0.037$ for these two suites (Figure~\ref{fig:r2_collapse}).
64	Across all six TracVLA and NORA cells, every VLM-to-VLA transition produces exit collapse without exception.
65	
66	OpenVLA~\cite{kim2024_openvla} presents a contrasting pattern.
67	Only the Object suite shows clear collapse: trained $\Delta R^2 = 0.121$ (peak $0.787$, exit $0.666$) vs.\ untrained $0.076$ (peak $0.761$, exit $0.685$).
68	Goal ($\Delta R^2 = 0.016$ trained vs.\ $0.033$ untrained) and Long-Horizon ($0.004$ vs.\ $0.016$) show near-zero trained collapse; in both cases the untrained model produces a larger peak-to-exit drop than the trained model.
69	This asymmetry reflects the nature of the comparison: OpenVLA's untrained checkpoint is the OXE-pretrained VLA~\cite{padalkar2023_oxe}, which has undergone 970K episodes of action training.
70	The OXE-to-LIBERO transition, a VLA-to-VLA comparison, produces collapse in only 1 of 3 cells.
71	
72	The contrast between VLM-to-VLA (6/6) and VLA-to-VLA (1/3) collapse rates clarifies the nature of exit-layer reorganization.
73	A one-sided sign test confirms that the VLM-to-VLA collapse direction is consistent: all six cells show trained $\Delta R^2 >$ untrained $\Delta R^2$ ($p = 0.016$).
74	$R^2$ exit collapse emerges when vision-language models are first fine-tuned into VLAs (6/6 cells across two architectures) but does not intensify with further task-specific training of already-pretrained VLAs (1/3 cells), identifying exit collapse as a one-time reorganization at the VLM-to-VLA transition.
75	Once a VLM has been transformed into a VLA through initial action training, exit-layer $R^2$ profiles are largely established.
76	The OpenVLA Object exception may reflect specific demands of object-centric manipulation, but the 6/6 vs.\ 1/3 contrast supports the transition-specific interpretation.

117	\subsection{Cross-Architecture Counterfactual Sensitivity}
118	\label{sec:cf_sensitivity}
119	
120	Counterfactual sensitivity provides a complementary measure of how trained VLAs integrate instruction information.
121	We replace the instruction with four perturbation types (empty, wrong task, shuffled tokens, paraphrased) and measure the resulting action divergence.
122	Table~\ref{tab:counterfactual} reports condition rankings for all eight cells where Cohen's $d$ is available (OpenVLA and TracVLA across four suites each).
123	Across both architectures and all eight combinations, every perturbation condition produces statistically significant action divergence ($d \geq 0.45$); trained VLAs are sensitive to instruction content regardless of perturbation type.
124	
125	The ``empty'' condition ranks first in 7 of 8 cells, with effect sizes from $d = 0.94$ (OpenVLA Spatial) to $1.52$ (TracVLA Goal).
126	OpenVLA Long-Horizon is the sole exception: ``shuffled'' ranks first ($d = 0.56$) and all conditions produce weaker effects ($d = 0.45$--$0.56$).
127	The remaining conditions follow a broadly consistent ordering: ``wrong'' and ``shuffled'' alternate in second and third position, while ``paraphrased'' ranks last in 7 of 8 cells.
128	TracVLA produces systematically higher effect sizes than OpenVLA ($d = 0.97$--$1.52$ vs.\ $0.45$--$1.21$), consistent with the Phi-3 backbone routing instruction information more strongly through the VLA pipeline.
129	NORA's counterfactual analysis uses cosine distance rather than Cohen's $d$ because its output format precludes action-level MSE computation.
130	NORA Goal produces saturated exit-layer cosine distances of $1.0$ for all conditions, with differentiation visible only at earlier layers (L24: wrong $= 0.123$, empty $= 0.098$).
131	NORA Spatial produces a peak cosine distance of $0.275$ for the ``wrong'' condition.
132	
133	\paragraph{Metric constraints on trained--untrained comparison.}
134	A critical limitation constrains quantitative comparison between trained and untrained counterfactual sensitivity.
135	Trained models produce action outputs, enabling Cohen's $d$ on action MSE (OpenVLA, TracVLA) or cosine distance on action tokens (NORA).
136	Untrained VLMs (Phi-3-Vision, Qwen2.5-VL) do not generate actions; their sensitivity is measured via cosine distance on hidden representations---a metric with different scale, units, and distributional properties.
137	Ratios between Cohen's $d$ and cosine distance are therefore methodologically invalid, and we do not report cross-metric amplification factors.
138	
139	Qualitatively, untrained VLMs show weak instruction sensitivity: TracVLA untrained (Phi-3-Vision) produces peak cosine distances of $0.15$--$0.19$ across four suites, and NORA untrained (Qwen2.5-VL) yields $0.081$ on Goal.
140	All trained models produce substantial sensitivity (Cohen's $d \geq 0.45$ for OpenVLA and TracVLA; cosine distances up to saturation for NORA), but the trained--untrained gap cannot be quantified as a single ratio.
141	
142	The one cell permitting same-metric comparison is OpenVLA Long-Horizon, where both the trained and the OXE-pretrained untrained checkpoints produce actions and are measured via Cohen's $d$.
143	The result is \emph{inverted}: the OXE-pretrained model ($d = 1.05$, empty) shows stronger sensitivity than the LIBERO-trained model ($d = 0.56$, shuffled; $0.50$, empty).
144	This inversion is consistent with OpenVLA Long's anomalous profile (near-zero $R^2$ collapse, lowest trained CF sensitivity in the matrix) and with the general-purpose OXE model maintaining broader instruction responsiveness than a task-specialized fine-tune.
145	
146	We conclude that VLA training produces consistent instruction sensitivity across architectures (all trained Cohen's $d \geq 0.45$; condition ordering preserved), but the magnitude of trained-versus-untrained change cannot be reliably quantified due to metric incomparability at the VLM-to-VLA transition.
147	Unlike $R^2$ exit collapse, counterfactual sensitivity is not limited to the VLM-to-VLA transition: trained OpenVLA produces $d = 0.98$ (Goal) and $1.21$ (Object), and the OXE-pretrained baseline for Object yields cosine distance $0.569$, indicating that task-specific training can modulate sensitivity within the VLA-to-VLA regime as well.

172	\subsection{L1 Attention Reflects Base-Model Priors}
173	\label{sec:l1_priors}
174	
175	L1 instruction-dominant head counts across architectures reveal a pattern that contrasts with the training-induced effects documented in \S\ref{sec:r2_collapse} and \S\ref{sec:cf_sensitivity}.
176	TracVLA untrained (Phi-3-Vision) allocates 32/32 heads to instruction-dominant attention across all four suites, saturating the capacity of its 32-head L1 before any VLA training.
177	Training slightly \emph{reduces} this count to 27--30/32, with freed heads presumably repurposed for action-related computation.
178	NORA untrained (Qwen2.5-VL) allocates 13--14 of its 16 L1 heads to instruction dominance (81--88\%), and training leaves this essentially unchanged at 12--13/16.
179	OpenVLA shows 24--26/32 instruction-dominant heads in the OXE-pretrained baseline; trained values are similar (14--24/32), with the largest change in Long-Horizon where training reduces the count from 25 to 14 heads (Figure~\ref{fig:cross_arch_l1}).
180	
181	These patterns are consistent with L1 instruction attention reflecting base-model language pretraining rather than VLA fine-tuning.
182	If VLA training were the primary driver of L1 instruction routing, untrained VLMs should show low instruction attention that increases after training, as observed in OpenVLA's random-weight condition (0/32 heads, \S\ref{sec:openvla_routing}).
183	Instead, TracVLA and NORA untrained models exhibit strong instruction attention before any action training.
184	Phi-3-Vision saturates at 32/32 heads ($100\%$) and Qwen2.5-VL allocates 13--14/16 ($81$--$88\%$), proportions characteristic of instruction-tuned language models that attend heavily to text tokens as part of their base training.
185	The fact that one backbone (Phi-3-Vision) exhibits fully saturated instruction attention even before fine-tuning provides the clearest evidence that L1 patterns are base-model priors.
186	This observation distinguishes two classes of routing effects: training-induced effects ($R^2$ exit collapse, counterfactual sensitivity) that emerge during VLA fine-tuning, and inherited effects (L1 instruction attention) that trace to base-model pretraining.
187	High L1 instruction attention does not indicate that a model has learned to route instructions for action prediction; it indicates that the base language model already devoted attention capacity to text tokens.
188

197	\subsection{Synthesis: Training-Induced vs.\ Inherited Routing}
198	\label{sec:routing_synthesis}
199	
200	The findings from \S\ref{sec:r2_collapse}--\ref{sec:l1_priors} distinguish two classes of routing effects.
201	Training-induced effects---$R^2$ exit collapse and counterfactual sensitivity---emerge or intensify at the VLM-to-VLA transition: exit collapse is present in 6/6 VLM-to-VLA cells (sign test $p = 0.016$) but only 1/3 VLA-to-VLA cells, and all trained models exhibit substantial counterfactual sensitivity ($d \geq 0.45$ where Cohen's $d$ is applicable).
202	Inherited effects---L1 instruction-dominant attention---trace to base-model language pretraining and persist through VLA fine-tuning (TracVLA: 32/32 before training; NORA: 13--14/16).
203	This distinction clarifies the representational role of VLA fine-tuning: training reorganizes mid-to-exit layer action encoding and establishes instruction-conditioned action sensitivity, while early-layer attention structure reflects the pretrained backbone.
204	The consistency of these training-induced effects across two VLM-to-VLA transitions (TracVLA, NORA)---architectures with dramatically different base-model priors---is compatible with exit collapse and counterfactual sensitivity reflecting task-structure constraints of VLA fine-tuning rather than architecture-specific artifacts; OpenVLA's partial confirmation (2/4 suites for $R^2$ collapse) tempers the generality of this interpretation.
205	A more detailed characterization of how these effects compose across training stages is developed in the Discussion (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).
206	
207	As a secondary observation, vision encoder geometry measured by RSA shows a non-monotonic profile with a middle-layer peak (L12: $\rho = 0.628$), and standalone DINOv2~\cite{oquab2024_dinov2} achieves the highest RSA among encoders ($\rho = 0.692$).
208	Under linear CKA~\cite{kornblith2019}, this non-monotonic pattern disappears (monotonic increase), qualifying the observation as metric-dependent (Appendix~\ref{sec:cka_appendix}).

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:setup}

We analyze three VLA architectures across four LIBERO~\cite{liu2023_libero} task suites (Goal, Spatial, Object, Long-Horizon) in a $3 \times 4$ cross-architecture matrix (Table~\ref{tab:cross_arch_matrix}).
The architectures span distinct backbone families: OpenVLA~\cite{kim2024_openvla,karamcheti2024} (Llama-2-7B~\cite{touvron2023_llama2}, 32 layers, 32 MHA heads), TracVLA~\cite{zheng2024tracevla} (Phi-3-mini~\cite{abdin2024phi3}, 32 layers, 32 heads), and NORA~\cite{TODO_nora} (Qwen2.5-VL-3B, 36 layers, GQA with 16 query heads and 2 KV heads).
Of the 12 matrix cells, 10 are filled; NORA Object and Long-Horizon lack available checkpoints.
Each architecture is compared in trained and untrained conditions, with a critical asymmetry between untrained baselines: OpenVLA's untrained checkpoint is the OXE-pretrained~\cite{padalkar2023_oxe} VLA (already fine-tuned for action prediction on 970K episodes), while TracVLA and NORA untrained checkpoints are pure vision-language models (Phi-3-Vision and Qwen2.5-VL) with no action training.
Three analyses are applied to each cell (\S\ref{sec:method}): $R^2$ action probes at all layers, L1 attention head profiling for instruction dominance, and counterfactual instruction perturbation.
For OpenVLA LIBERO-Goal, $N = 63{,}228$ observations; other cells are at comparable scale.
For trained models that produce action outputs, counterfactual sensitivity is measured via Cohen's $d$ on action MSE.
For untrained VLMs (Phi-3-Vision, Qwen2.5-VL) that do not produce actions, sensitivity is measured via cosine distance on hidden representations; these metrics operate on different scales and are not directly comparable (\S\ref{sec:cf_sensitivity}).
OpenVLA's OXE-pretrained checkpoint produces actions, permitting same-metric (Cohen's $d$) comparison in that condition.
Bonferroni correction details appear in Appendix~\ref{sec:bonferroni_correction}.

%------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{OpenVLA: Instruction Routing and Functional Sensitivity}
\label{sec:openvla_routing}

We first establish the core phenomena on a single architecture before testing cross-architectural generality.
Cross-instruction probes validate the analysis framework on OpenVLA~\cite{kim2024_openvla}: as predicted by the causal mask, image\_mean instruction classification stays at chance ($10\%$) across all 32 layers in all conditions (full profile in Appendix~\ref{sec:dense_routing}).
Trained readout achieves $100\%$ 10-way classification from L1 onward and maintains this through L31 (LOOCV-confirmed; Appendix~\ref{sec:loocv}).
Untrained readout also reaches $100\%$ at L1 but decays to $82\%$ by L31; the readout token is thus the primary multimodal integration site, and training stabilizes its instruction encoding across depth.
All patterns reproduce with a linear probe (Appendix~\ref{sec:linear_probe}).

At L1, three conditions form a gradient of instruction attention: untrained networks allocate 0/32 instruction-dominant heads ($11.7\%$ text attention, $1.5\times$ text-to-image ratio), Llama-2 base~\cite{touvron2023_llama2} allocates 9/32 ($36.5\%$), and VLA-trained allocates 24/32 ($57.7\%$, $38.2\times$ text-to-image ratio; Appendix~\ref{sec:attention_decomp}).
The 32-layer attention profile reveals qualitatively distinct organizations: Llama-2 base concentrates instruction attention at mid-depth (L9--L16: 15--22 heads), while VLA fine-tuning produces an entry-exit bookend pattern with L0--L1 at 21--24 heads, L31 at 18, and intermediate layers at 0--11 (Appendix~\ref{sec:threshold_sensitivity}).
Head counts are computed at a $50\%$ threshold; sensitivity analysis ($30\%$--$70\%$) confirms ordering robustness.
A fourth condition, OpenVLA fine-tuned on LIBERO, preserves L1 entry concentration (22/32 heads) but loses L31 exit re-engagement entirely (0 vs.\ 18 heads for the OXE-pretrained model), consistent with exit-layer attention serving multi-task flexibility rather than task-specific routing.
The redistribution beyond Llama-2 base priors confirms that VLA fine-tuning creates new instruction routing rather than merely inheriting language-model attention.

Counterfactual instruction perturbation validates the functional relevance of these structural patterns.
Four perturbation types across 10 LIBERO-Goal tasks produce action divergence ordered by token novelty ($\rho = 0.8$): empty instruction ($d = 0.978$), wrong task ($0.924$), shuffled tokens ($0.763$), paraphrased ($0.707$).
The shuffled-exceeds-paraphrased ordering, despite identical token sets, indicates that positional sensitivity dominates token-level novelty.
The effect replicates across LIBERO-Spatial (10 tasks) with the same ordering: empty $0.942$, wrong $0.851$, shuffled $0.833$, paraphrased $0.806$ (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:counterfactual_spatial}).
Across both suites (20 tasks), the gradient spans $d = 0.71$--$0.98$.
Spatial instructions differ only in prepositions, yet wrong-task perturbation still produces $d = 0.851$; instruction-dominant heads route fine-grained spatial information, not merely task identity.

Dose-response ablation of L1 instruction-dominant heads produces monotonic trajectory divergence: $d$ rises from $0.482$ to $0.639$ as 4--32 heads are progressively ablated, with steep increase through 12 heads and plateau beyond 20 (Appendix~\ref{sec:action_trajectory}).
Ablating all 24 instruction-dominant heads alters $72.3\%$ of action tokens (token-level $d = 0.65$, trajectory-level $d = 2.943$); control ablation of 8 random heads yields $d = 0.41$ ($29.3\%$ tokens affected), concentrated on the gripper dimension.
The routing effect is task-dependent: instruction-discriminative tasks show $2.5\times$ larger $|\Delta R^2|$ under L1 ablation than visually-sufficient tasks ($p = 0.033$; Appendix~\ref{sec:task_complexity}).
$R^2$ action probing localizes training effects: trained readout peaks at $R^2 = 0.678$ (L13), untrained readout peaks at $0.609$ (L32), and the training effect concentrates at the readout ($+0.069$) rather than at image\_mean ($+0.015$; Appendix~\ref{sec:action_r2_threecond}).
These effects survive Bonferroni correction across all 63 tests (Appendix~\ref{sec:bonferroni_correction}).
The single-architecture analysis establishes three phenomena for cross-architectural testing: instruction-dominant attention at L1, $R^2$ exit-layer dynamics between trained and untrained conditions, and graded counterfactual sensitivity to instruction perturbation.

\subsection{Cross-Architecture $R^2$ Exit Collapse}
\label{sec:r2_collapse}

We define $R^2$ exit collapse as the drop in action-probe $R^2$ from peak layer to exit layer ($\Delta R^2 = R^2_{\text{peak}} - R^2_{\text{exit}}$).
A large $\Delta R^2$ indicates that action-relevant information encoded at intermediate layers is selectively discarded or transformed before reaching the exit.
Table~\ref{tab:cross_arch_matrix} reports this quantity for all available cells in the $3 \times 4$ matrix.
A consistent pattern emerges: trained models exhibit substantially larger $\Delta R^2$ than their untrained counterparts, but the magnitude and prevalence of collapse depend on the training transition being measured.

TracVLA~\cite{zheng2024tracevla} shows clear exit collapse across all four LIBERO suites.
Trained $\Delta R^2$ ranges from $0.138$ (Spatial: peak $R^2 = 0.809$, exit $0.671$) to $0.294$ (Object: peak $0.764$, exit $0.470$), while untrained $\Delta R^2$ is uniformly small, from $0.009$ (Object) to $0.048$ (Goal).
The untrained TracVLA checkpoint is Phi-3-Vision, a pure vision-language model with no action training, and its flat $R^2$ profiles confirm that exit collapse is absent before VLA fine-tuning.
NORA~\cite{TODO_nora} exhibits the most extreme collapse in the matrix.
LIBERO-Goal trained produces $\Delta R^2 = 0.691$: the profile peaks at $R^2 = 0.688$ in mid-layers and drops to $-0.004$ at exit, below chance, so exit-layer representations encode less action-relevant structure than random vectors.
LIBERO-Spatial yields $\Delta R^2 = 0.302$ (peak $0.720$, exit $0.417$).
NORA untrained (Qwen2.5-VL) produces $\Delta R^2$ of only $0.044$ and $0.037$ for these two suites (Figure~\ref{fig:r2_collapse}).
Across all six TracVLA and NORA cells, every VLM-to-VLA transition produces exit collapse without exception.

OpenVLA~\cite{kim2024_openvla} presents a contrasting pattern.
Only the Object suite shows clear collapse: trained $\Delta R^2 = 0.121$ (peak $0.787$, exit $0.666$) vs.\ untrained $0.076$ (peak $0.761$, exit $0.685$).
Goal ($\Delta R^2 = 0.016$ trained vs.\ $0.033$ untrained) and Long-Horizon ($0.004$ vs.\ $0.016$) show near-zero trained collapse; in both cases the untrained model produces a larger peak-to-exit drop than the trained model.
This asymmetry reflects the nature of the comparison: OpenVLA's untrained checkpoint is the OXE-pretrained VLA~\cite{padalkar2023_oxe}, which has undergone 970K episodes of action training.
The OXE-to-LIBERO transition, a VLA-to-VLA comparison, produces collapse in only 1 of 3 cells.

The contrast between VLM-to-VLA (6/6) and VLA-to-VLA (1/3) collapse rates clarifies the nature of exit-layer reorganization.
A one-sided sign test confirms that the VLM-to-VLA collapse direction is consistent: all six cells show trained $\Delta R^2 >$ untrained $\Delta R^2$ ($p = 0.016$).
$R^2$ exit collapse emerges when vision-language models are first fine-tuned into VLAs (6/6 cells across two architectures) but does not intensify with further task-specific training of already-pretrained VLAs (1/3 cells), identifying exit collapse as a one-time reorganization at the VLM-to-VLA transition.
Once a VLM has been transformed into a VLA through initial action training, exit-layer $R^2$ profiles are largely established.
The OpenVLA Object exception may reflect specific demands of object-centric manipulation, but the 6/6 vs.\ 1/3 contrast supports the transition-specific interpretation.

\subsection{Cross-Architecture Counterfactual Sensitivity}
\label{sec:cf_sensitivity}

Counterfactual sensitivity provides a complementary measure of how trained VLAs integrate instruction information.
We replace the instruction with four perturbation types (empty, wrong task, shuffled tokens, paraphrased) and measure the resulting action divergence.
Table~\ref{tab:counterfactual} reports condition rankings for all eight cells where Cohen's $d$ is available (OpenVLA and TracVLA across four suites each).
Across both architectures and all eight combinations, every perturbation condition produces statistically significant action divergence ($d \geq 0.45$); trained VLAs are sensitive to instruction content regardless of perturbation type.

The ``empty'' condition ranks first in 7 of 8 cells, with effect sizes from $d = 0.94$ (OpenVLA Spatial) to $1.52$ (TracVLA Goal).
OpenVLA Long-Horizon is the sole exception: ``shuffled'' ranks first ($d = 0.56$) and all conditions produce weaker effects ($d = 0.45$--$0.56$).
The remaining conditions follow a broadly consistent ordering: ``wrong'' and ``shuffled'' alternate in second and third position, while ``paraphrased'' ranks last in 7 of 8 cells.
TracVLA produces systematically higher effect sizes than OpenVLA ($d = 0.97$--$1.52$ vs.\ $0.45$--$1.21$), consistent with the Phi-3 backbone routing instruction information more strongly through the VLA pipeline.
NORA's counterfactual analysis uses cosine distance rather than Cohen's $d$ because its output format precludes action-level MSE computation.
NORA Goal produces saturated exit-layer cosine distances of $1.0$ for all conditions, with differentiation visible only at earlier layers (L24: wrong $= 0.123$, empty $= 0.098$).
NORA Spatial produces a peak cosine distance of $0.275$ for the ``wrong'' condition.

\paragraph{Metric constraints on trained--untrained comparison.}
A critical limitation constrains quantitative comparison between trained and untrained counterfactual sensitivity.
Trained models produce action outputs, enabling Cohen's $d$ on action MSE (OpenVLA, TracVLA) or cosine distance on action tokens (NORA).
Untrained VLMs (Phi-3-Vision, Qwen2.5-VL) do not generate actions; their sensitivity is measured via cosine distance on hidden representations---a metric with different scale, units, and distributional properties.
Ratios between Cohen's $d$ and cosine distance are therefore methodologically invalid, and we do not report cross-metric amplification factors.

Qualitatively, untrained VLMs show weak instruction sensitivity: TracVLA untrained (Phi-3-Vision) produces peak cosine distances of $0.15$--$0.19$ across four suites, and NORA untrained (Qwen2.5-VL) yields $0.081$ on Goal.
All trained models produce substantial sensitivity (Cohen's $d \geq 0.45$ for OpenVLA and TracVLA; cosine distances up to saturation for NORA), but the trained--untrained gap cannot be quantified as a single ratio.

The one cell permitting same-metric comparison is OpenVLA Long-Horizon, where both the trained and the OXE-pretrained untrained checkpoints produce actions and are measured via Cohen's $d$.
The result is \emph{inverted}: the OXE-pretrained model ($d = 1.05$, empty) shows stronger sensitivity than the LIBERO-trained model ($d = 0.56$, shuffled; $0.50$, empty).
This inversion is consistent with OpenVLA Long's anomalous profile (near-zero $R^2$ collapse, lowest trained CF sensitivity in the matrix) and with the general-purpose OXE model maintaining broader instruction responsiveness than a task-specialized fine-tune.

We conclude that VLA training produces consistent instruction sensitivity across architectures (all trained Cohen's $d \geq 0.45$; condition ordering preserved), but the magnitude of trained-versus-untrained change cannot be reliably quantified due to metric incomparability at the VLM-to-VLA transition.
Unlike $R^2$ exit collapse, counterfactual sensitivity is not limited to the VLM-to-VLA transition: trained OpenVLA produces $d = 0.98$ (Goal) and $1.21$ (Object), and the OXE-pretrained baseline for Object yields cosine distance $0.569$, indicating that task-specific training can modulate sensitivity within the VLA-to-VLA regime as well.

\subsection{L1 Attention Reflects Base-Model Priors}
\label{sec:l1_priors}

L1 instruction-dominant head counts across architectures reveal a pattern that contrasts with the training-induced effects documented in \S\ref{sec:r2_collapse} and \S\ref{sec:cf_sensitivity}.
TracVLA untrained (Phi-3-Vision) allocates 32/32 heads to instruction-dominant attention across all four suites, saturating the capacity of its 32-head L1 before any VLA training.
Training slightly \emph{reduces} this count to 27--30/32, with freed heads presumably repurposed for action-related computation.
NORA untrained (Qwen2.5-VL) allocates 13--14 of its 16 L1 heads to instruction dominance (81--88\%), and training leaves this essentially unchanged at 12--13/16.
OpenVLA shows 24--26/32 instruction-dominant heads in the OXE-pretrained baseline; trained values are similar (14--24/32), with the largest change in Long-Horizon where training reduces the count from 25 to 14 heads (Figure~\ref{fig:cross_arch_l1}).

These patterns are consistent with L1 instruction attention reflecting base-model language pretraining rather than VLA fine-tuning.
If VLA training were the primary driver of L1 instruction routing, untrained VLMs should show low instruction attention that increases after training, as observed in OpenVLA's random-weight condition (0/32 heads, \S\ref{sec:openvla_routing}).
Instead, TracVLA and NORA untrained models exhibit strong instruction attention before any action training.
Phi-3-Vision saturates at 32/32 heads ($100\%$) and Qwen2.5-VL allocates 13--14/16 ($81$--$88\%$), proportions characteristic of instruction-tuned language models that attend heavily to text tokens as part of their base training.
The fact that one backbone (Phi-3-Vision) exhibits fully saturated instruction attention even before fine-tuning provides the clearest evidence that L1 patterns are base-model priors.
This observation distinguishes two classes of routing effects: training-induced effects ($R^2$ exit collapse, counterfactual sensitivity) that emerge during VLA fine-tuning, and inherited effects (L1 instruction attention) that trace to base-model pretraining.
High L1 instruction attention does not indicate that a model has learned to route instructions for action prediction; it indicates that the base language model already devoted attention capacity to text tokens.

\subsection{Synthesis: Training-Induced vs.\ Inherited Routing}
\label{sec:routing_synthesis}

The findings from \S\ref{sec:r2_collapse}--\ref{sec:l1_priors} distinguish two classes of routing effects.
Training-induced effects---$R^2$ exit collapse and counterfactual sensitivity---emerge or intensify at the VLM-to-VLA transition: exit collapse is present in 6/6 VLM-to-VLA cells (sign test $p = 0.016$) but only 1/3 VLA-to-VLA cells, and all trained models exhibit substantial counterfactual sensitivity ($d \geq 0.45$ where Cohen's $d$ is applicable).
Inherited effects---L1 instruction-dominant attention---trace to base-model language pretraining and persist through VLA fine-tuning (TracVLA: 32/32 before training; NORA: 13--14/16).
This distinction clarifies the representational role of VLA fine-tuning: training reorganizes mid-to-exit layer action encoding and establishes instruction-conditioned action sensitivity, while early-layer attention structure reflects the pretrained backbone.
The consistency of these training-induced effects across two VLM-to-VLA transitions (TracVLA, NORA)---architectures with dramatically different base-model priors---is compatible with exit collapse and counterfactual sensitivity reflecting task-structure constraints of VLA fine-tuning rather than architecture-specific artifacts; OpenVLA's partial confirmation (2/4 suites for $R^2$ collapse) tempers the generality of this interpretation.
A more detailed characterization of how these effects compose across training stages is developed in the Discussion (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).

As a secondary observation, vision encoder geometry measured by RSA shows a non-monotonic profile with a middle-layer peak (L12: $\rho = 0.628$), and standalone DINOv2~\cite{oquab2024_dinov2} achieves the highest RSA among encoders ($\rho = 0.692$).
Under linear CKA~\cite{kornblith2019}, this non-monotonic pattern disappears (monotonic increase), qualifying the observation as metric-dependent (Appendix~\ref{sec:cka_appendix}).

\section{Method}
\label{sec:method}

We investigate how action-relevant representations are organized across three VLA architectures using complementary probing, attention, and perturbation analyses.

%------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Architectures and Data}
\label{sec:arch_data}

We study three VLAs that span distinct backbone families (Table~\ref{tab:arch_overview}).
\textbf{OpenVLA}~\cite{kim2024_openvla,karamcheti2024} chains a frozen DinoSigLIP vision backbone~\cite{zhai2023_siglip,oquab2024_dinov2} (DINOv2 ViT-L/14 + SigLIP-SO400M), an MLP projector (2{,}176-D $\to$ 4{,}096-D), and Llama-2-7B~\cite{touvron2023_llama2} (6.74B parameters, 32 layers, 32 multi-head attention [MHA] heads) for autoregressive 7-D action decoding.
Its base checkpoint is pretrained on Open X-Embodiment~\cite{padalkar2023_oxe} (OXE; 970K episodes across multiple robot platforms).
\textbf{TracVLA}~\cite{zheng2024tracevla} uses Phi-3-mini~\cite{abdin2024phi3} (32 layers, 32 MHA heads) with a SigLIP encoder augmented by spatial trace conditioning, trained on an OXE subset.
\textbf{NORA}~\cite{TODO_nora} uses Qwen2.5-VL-3B (36 layers, grouped-query attention [GQA] with 16 query heads and 2 KV heads) with its native vision encoder.

Each architecture is evaluated in trained and untrained conditions.
A critical asymmetry distinguishes the untrained baselines: OpenVLA's untrained checkpoint is the OXE-pretrained VLA, already fine-tuned for action prediction on 970K episodes, while TracVLA and NORA untrained checkpoints are pure vision-language models (Phi-3-Vision and Qwen2.5-VL) with no action training.
OpenVLA trained-vs-untrained comparisons therefore measure a VLA-to-VLA transition; TracVLA and NORA comparisons measure VLM-to-VLA transitions.
This asymmetry affects the interpretation of all trained/untrained comparisons throughout the paper.
For OpenVLA, two additional conditions support deep-dive analyses (\S\ref{sec:openvla_routing}): the Llama-2 base language model (no VLA fine-tuning) and a random-weight initialization via \texttt{from\_config()}.

We evaluate on LIBERO~\cite{liu2023_libero}, comprising four task suites (Goal, Spatial, Object, Long-Horizon) with 10 tasks and 50 demonstrations each.
The three architectures and four suites form a $3 \times 4$ matrix; 10 of 12 cells are filled (NORA Object and Long-Horizon lack available checkpoints).

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Architectures studied. The untrained baselines differ in kind: OpenVLA's baseline is an OXE-pretrained VLA that produces actions; TracVLA and NORA baselines are pure VLMs with no action training.}
\label{tab:arch_overview}
\footnotesize
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llccll@{}}
\toprule
Arch. & Backbone & Layers & Attention & Vision Enc. & Untrained Baseline \\
\midrule
OpenVLA & Llama-2-7B & 32 & 32 MHA & DinoSigLIP $\to$ MLP proj. & OXE-pret.\ VLA \\
TracVLA & Phi-3-mini & 32 & 32 MHA & SigLIP + spatial trace & Phi-3-Vision (VLM) \\
NORA & Qwen2.5-VL-3B & 36 & 16q/2kv GQA & Qwen2.5-VL native & Qwen2.5-VL (VLM) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

%------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Representation Extraction}
\label{sec:repr_extraction}

From each architecture, we extract hidden states at every transformer layer from two token positions: (a)~\textbf{image\_mean}, the mean activation over image tokens, and (b)~\textbf{readout}, the hidden state at the final pre-action token, which follows both image and instruction tokens in the causal sequence and can attend to all preceding context.
L0 denotes the embedding layer output, L1 through L$N$ the hidden states after each transformer layer ($N = 32$ for OpenVLA and TracVLA, $N = 36$ for NORA), with the final layer including the output layer norm.
In all three architectures, image tokens precede instruction tokens; the causal mask prevents image tokens from attending to instructions by construction.

We cross two factors in a $2 \times 2$ factorial design: \emph{training status} (trained vs.\ untrained) and \emph{instruction presence} (with vs.\ without task description), applied to all 10 available cells in the cross-architecture matrix.
OpenVLA additionally provides representations from the DinoSigLIP projector output (4{,}096-D), DINOv2 and CLIP external baselines, and the branch-split before fusion; these sources support the OpenVLA deep-dive analyses (\S\ref{sec:openvla_routing}).

%------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Cross-Architecture Analyses}
\label{sec:cross_arch_analyses}

Three analyses are applied to every available cell in the $3 \times 4$ matrix.

\paragraph{$R^2$ action probes.}
Two-layer MLP probes~\cite{alain2017} ($d_\text{in} \to 256 \to 7$, ReLU) are trained to predict 7-D action vectors from frozen representations at each layer (Adam, lr${}=10^{-3}$, batch size 256, 50 epochs, early stopping patience 5).
Train/test splits follow demonstration boundaries (demos 0--39 vs.\ 40--49) to prevent within-trajectory leakage.
We report per-task macro-averaged $R^2$ with bootstrap paired comparisons (10{,}000 resamples).

\paragraph{L1 attention head profiling.}
At L1, each attention head is classified as instruction-dominant ($>50\%$ of readout-token attention allocated to instruction tokens) or image-dominant.
Results are reported as $k/N$ instruction-dominant heads, where $N$ is the total L1 head count: 32 for OpenVLA and TracVLA (MHA), 16 for NORA (GQA query heads).
Sensitivity analysis at thresholds from $30\%$ to $70\%$ confirms ordering robustness (Appendix~\ref{sec:threshold_sensitivity}).

\paragraph{Counterfactual instruction perturbation.}
The instruction is replaced with four conditions: empty string, wrong task from the same suite, shuffled tokens, and paraphrased instruction.
A metric constraint arises from the trained/untrained asymmetry.
Trained models produce action outputs; their sensitivity is measured via Cohen's $d$ on action MSE (OpenVLA, TracVLA) or cosine distance on action representations (NORA).
Untrained VLMs (Phi-3-Vision, Qwen2.5-VL) do not generate actions; their sensitivity is measured via cosine distance on hidden representations, a metric with different scale and distributional properties.
Cross-metric ratios between Cohen's $d$ and cosine distance are therefore invalid (\S\ref{sec:cf_sensitivity}).
OpenVLA's OXE-pretrained untrained checkpoint is the exception: because it produces actions, same-metric (Cohen's $d$) trained-vs-untrained comparison is possible for that condition.

%------------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{OpenVLA-Specific Analyses}
\label{sec:openvla_analyses}

Three additional analyses are applied to OpenVLA to characterize instruction encoding and representational geometry.

\paragraph{Cross-instruction probes.}
Each visual frame is paired with all 10 LIBERO-Goal task instructions, producing 10 representation vectors per frame per layer.
A 10-way linear classifier identifies which instruction was present, applied separately to image\_mean and readout positions, with leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) over 10 folds.

\paragraph{Representational similarity analysis (RSA).}
RSA~\cite{kriegeskorte2008} quantifies geometric alignment between representations and the action space.
For each task, we compute pairwise representational dissimilarity matrices (RDMs) using cosine distances for representations and Euclidean distances for 7-D action vectors, from within-task observation pairs across 50 demonstrations.
Alignment is measured via Spearman $\rho$ between upper-triangular RDM entries; we report mean $\rho$ across 10 tasks with 95\% confidence intervals from 10{,}000 bootstrap resamples at the task level~\cite{nili2014toolbox}.
We prefer RSA over CKA~\cite{kornblith2019}: RSA captures relative distance structure via scale-invariant rank correlation, suited to comparing high- and low-dimensional spaces (4{,}096-D vs.\ 7-D), while CKA measures global subspace overlap that can remain high when geometric structure differs.
Both metrics are reported in Appendix~\ref{sec:cka_appendix}; their divergence (\S\ref{sec:routing_synthesis}) confirms that neither alone fully characterizes representational structure.

\paragraph{External baselines.}
DINOv2 ViT-L/14~\cite{oquab2024_dinov2} (\texttt{cls\_token}/\texttt{patch\_mean}) and CLIP ViT-L/14~\cite{radford2021_clip} (\texttt{patch\_mean}) provide self-supervised and vision-language pretrained reference points for probing and RSA.
